subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The UK's physical and human challenges

questions.q: Which of the following is a process of coastal TRANSPORTATION rather than erosion?
questions.explain: Longshore drift moves sediment along a coastline, whereas hydraulic action, abrasion and attrition all wear rock away.

questions.q: Chalk, which forms many of the UK's coastal cliffs, is classified as which rock type?
questions.explain: Chalk is a soft sedimentary rock formed from compressed marine deposits.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence in which erosional features develop along a headland?
questions.explain: A crack is widened into a cave, which erodes through the headland to form an arch, then collapses to leave a stack that is worn down to a stump.

questions.q: An oxbow lake is formed when...
options: A waterfall retreats upstream and leaves a gorge
The narrow neck of a meander is eroded through, cutting off a loop
Sediment is deposited on the inside bend of a river
A river overflows its banks and deposits levées
questions.explain: Continued erosion narrows a meander neck until the river breaks through, abandoning the loop as a crescent-shaped oxbow lake.

questions.q: Which set of features is typical of the UPPER course of a UK river?
options: Vertical erosion and a steep V-shaped valley
Lateral erosion and a wide floodplain
Deposition of silt forming natural levées
questions.explain: In the upper course the river cuts downwards (vertical erosion), creating a steep-sided V-shaped valley.

questions.q: A coastal town on a rapidly retreating cliff of soft boulder clay wants to protect the base of the cliff from wave attack. Which hard-engineering option does this MOST directly?
questions.explain: A sea wall is built against the cliff base to absorb and reflect wave energy, directly protecting it from erosion.

questions.q: Which UK employment sector is described as the quaternary sector?
options: Extraction of raw materials such as mining
Providing services such as retail and healthcare
questions.explain: The quaternary sector involves high-tech research, information and knowledge-based work.

questions.q: Deindustrialisation in the UK refers to...
options: People moving from cities to the countryside
questions.explain: Deindustrialisation is the fall in importance and employment of the manufacturing/secondary sector.

questions.q: The most economically prosperous 'core' region of the UK is generally regarded as...
questions.explain: London and the South East form the UK's economic core, with higher wages, investment and employment than peripheral regions.

questions.q: Counter-urbanisation is the movement of people...
options: From rural areas into large cities
From cities into surrounding rural or suburban areas
questions.explain: Counter-urbanisation is the movement of people out of cities to live in rural and suburban locations.

questions.q: Which of these energy sources used in the UK is renewable?
questions.explain: Wind is a renewable resource, whereas gas and coal are fossil fuels and nuclear relies on finite uranium.

questions.q: Within the UK, areas of water SURPLUS and water DEFICIT are best described as...
options: Surplus in the wetter north and west; deficit in the drier, populous south and east
Surplus in the south east; deficit in the north west
Surplus everywhere, so no transfers are needed
questions.explain: The north and west receive more rainfall and have lower demand, while the south and east are drier but more densely populated.

questions.q: A water transfer scheme involves moving water...
options: From areas of surplus to areas of deficit
From deficit areas to surplus areas
questions.explain: Water transfers pipe or channel water from regions with a surplus to regions where demand exceeds supply.

questions.q: Fracking (hydraulic fracturing) is a method used to extract...
questions.explain: Fracking injects high-pressure fluid into shale rock to release trapped natural (shale) gas.

questions.q: Over recent decades the UK's electricity mix has mainly shifted...
options: From coal towards gas and renewables
questions.explain: The UK has phased out coal, increasing the share of natural gas and renewable sources such as wind.

questions.q: The term 'food miles' refers to...
options: The distance food travels from producer to consumer
The calories contained in imported food
The area of farmland needed to feed a city
The cost of importing food per tonne
questions.explain: Food miles measure the distance food is transported, which is linked to carbon emissions.

questions.q: During a dry summer, households in south-east England are placed under a hosepipe ban. This is most directly a symptom of...
questions.explain: A hosepipe ban shows demand for water is outstripping supply, indicating water deficit or stress.

questions.q: In a geographical decision-making exercise, a 'stakeholder' is...
options: An individual or group with an interest in the decision
questions.explain: Stakeholders are the people, groups or organisations affected by, or with an interest in, a proposal.

questions.q: In geography, 'synoptic' thinking means...
options: Using only one piece of evidence
Drawing together and linking knowledge from different topics
Ignoring social factors in a decision
questions.explain: Synoptic skills involve connecting ideas from across the specification to reach a reasoned judgement.

questions.q: Sustainable development is best defined as development that...
options: Maximises short-term profit whatever the cost
Meets present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
questions.explain: Sustainability balances economic, social and environmental needs so that future generations are not disadvantaged.

questions.q: In a decision-making exercise, planners note that a proposed scheme would drain a wetland used by wading birds. This concern is best classified as which type of impact?
questions.explain: Loss of habitat and biodiversity is an environmental impact, one of the categories weighed in a balanced decision.

questions.q: A decision-making exercise compares four UK energy options. Which would generally be judged the MOST sustainable?
questions.explain: Offshore wind is renewable and low-carbon, making it more sustainable than fossil-fuel options.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Geography B (1GB0) specification; Geographical Investigations: UK Challenges
